title: War and peace
about: Collocations about how wars start and are fought (war broke out, fierce fighting, open fire), how peace is made and kept (call a ceasefire, sign a peace treaty, keep the peace), and war words in everyday life (a running battle, put up a fight, a price war).

items.pattern: war / fighting / a fire / a fight breaks out · when war broke out · the outbreak of war
items.meaning: a war (or a fire, a fight) suddenly starts
items.example: When **war broke out** in 1914, many people thought it would be over by Christmas.
more: A fire **broke out** in the hotel kitchen, but everyone got out safely.
A fight **broke out** in the queue when someone tried to push in.
items.watchOut: «Спалахнула війна» — war broke out, а не flashed up. Так само про пожежу, бійку, епідемію: a fire / a fight broke out. Не плутай з break down (зламатися) і break up (розійтися).

items.pattern: join the army / navy / air force · serve in the army · be in the army
items.meaning: become a soldier (or a sailor, a pilot) in your country's forces
items.uk: піти до армії, вступити на військову службу
items.example: In 1915 my great-great-grandfather left his farm and **joined the army**.
more: In the film, the hero **joins the navy** because he wants to see the world.
She **joined the air force** as a cook and ended up as a pilot.
items.watchOut: «Піти в армію» — join the army (або go into the army), а не go to the army. Служити в армії — serve in the army або be in the army.

items.pattern: declare war on a country / on sth · war is declared
items.meaning: officially say that you are starting a war; in everyday English, decide to fight a problem
items.example: In 1812 the United States **declared war on** Britain.
more: Our history teacher asked why the king had **declared war on** his own cousin.
Dad has **declared war on** the pigeons that eat his strawberries.
items.watchOut: «Оголосити війну» — declare war, а не announce war. Кому — зазвичай on: declare war on a country (не to).

items.pattern: go to war (with / against sb) (over sth)
items.meaning: start fighting a war against another country
items.example: In 1337 England and France **went to war** over who should rule France.
more: In the story, two kingdoms **go to war** over a stolen golden cup.
In Gulliver's Travels, two tiny countries **go to war** over which end of a boiled egg to break.
items.watchOut: Go to war — без артикля: країна вступає у війну. Про людину, яка вирушає воювати, частіше кажуть go off to war. Через що — over: go to war over land.

items.pattern: fierce / heavy fighting · a fierce battle · fierce competition
items.meaning: very violent fighting
items.example: There was **fierce fighting** at the castle gates for three days.
more: The film shows the **fierce fighting** at Waterloo without making it look glamorous.
Our guide pointed to the hill where the **heaviest fighting** took place.
items.watchOut: «Запеклі бої» — fierce або heavy fighting (fighting тут незлічуване, без -s), а не strong чи cruel fighting. Fierce читається /fɪəs/, одним складом.

items.pattern: a minor incident · only a few minor incidents · opposite: a serious / major incident
items.meaning: small events, such as small fights or accidents, that are not serious
items.example: Apart from a few **minor incidents**, the New Year celebrations in the city centre passed off peacefully.
more: It was just a **minor incident**: a bus scraped a parked car in the high street.
The school trip went well, with only one **minor incident**, when Sam's hat blew into the river.
items.watchOut: Incident — неприємна подія: сутичка, бійка, аварія. «Дрібний, незначний» тут найчастіше minor; протилежне — a serious або major incident.

items.pattern: all-out war · an all-out attack / effort · also full-scale war
items.meaning: a complete war, with all forces fighting, not just small fights; also a very serious quarrel
items.uk: справжня (тотальна) війна, війна на повну силу
items.example: When both twins wanted the top bunk, it was **all-out war**.
more: Historians still argue about why the quarrel between the two kingdoms turned into **all-out war**.
By the end of the meeting, the argument about the school uniform had become **all-out war**.
items.watchOut: All-out пишеться через дефіс і стоїть перед іменником: all-out war, an all-out effort (з усіх сил). Так само кажуть full-scale war.

items.pattern: come / be within (firing) range of sth · in / into range · out of range
items.meaning: close enough for guns (or arrows, water, a camera) to reach
items.uk: на відстані пострілу, у зоні досяжності (вогню)
items.example: The archers waited until the enemy came **within range**.
more: Don't stand **within range** of the garden sprinkler unless you want to get wet.
The ships stayed just **out of range** of the castle's cannons.
items.watchOut: «На відстані пострілу» — within range (of), а не on the distance of. Поза досяжністю — out of range. Range тут — дальність, а не «ранг».

items.pattern: open fire (on / at sb/sth) · hold your fire (wait, don't shoot)
items.meaning: start shooting
items.example: In the film, the pirates **open fire on** a passing ship.
more: At the start of the paintball game, the other team **opened fire** before we were ready.
At the history festival, the 'soldiers' **open fire** with blanks, and the children cover their ears.
items.watchOut: «Відкрити вогонь» — open fire, без артикля (не open the fire). По кому — on або at: opened fire on the ship. Light a fire — розпалити вогонь, багаття.

items.pattern: be taken prisoner · take sb prisoner · also be captured
items.meaning: be caught by the enemy and kept as a prisoner
items.example: On his way home from the Crusades, King Richard I **was taken prisoner** in Austria.
more: In the film, the hero **is taken prisoner** but escapes in a laundry basket.
Joan of Arc **was taken prisoner** in 1430 and handed over to the English.
items.watchOut: «Потрапити в полон» — be taken prisoner, без артикля: не taken a prisoner. Взяти в полон — take sb prisoner. Дослівне fell into captivity звучить книжно.

items.pattern: go into action · also swing / spring into action (start quickly)
items.meaning: start fighting; in everyday English, start doing something quickly and actively
items.uk: вступити в бій; узятися до справи
items.example: Tanks **went into action** for the first time in 1916.
more: As soon as the alarm sounded, the fire crew **went into action**.
When Grandma phoned to say she was coming, the whole family **went into action**: hoovering, dusting and baking.
items.watchOut: Go into action — без артикля (не into the action). Побачити когось у дії — see sb in action.

items.pattern: a decisive battle / moment / victory / factor
items.meaning: a battle that decides who wins the war
items.example: Hastings, in 1066, was a **decisive battle**: after it, England had a Norman king.
more: Our teacher asked which was the **decisive battle** of the war, and nobody knew.
The last match of the season was **decisive**: whoever won would take the cup.
items.watchOut: Decisive /dɪˈsaɪsɪv/ — вирішальний, наголос на другий склад. Decided — помітний, безсумнівний (a decided improvement). Про людину decisive — рішучий: a decisive leader.

items.pattern: a battle / storm / fire / argument rages (on) · a raging storm
items.meaning: a battle (or a storm, a fire, an argument) continues with great force
items.example: The battle **raged** all day, and by evening neither side had won.
more: A storm **raged** all night, and we lost power twice.
The argument about where to go on holiday **raged** in our house for a week.
items.watchOut: Rage тут — дієслово: a battle / storm / fire rages. Українською краще не «битва лютувала», а «точилася запекла битва», «вирувала буря».

items.pattern: fight a war / a battle (against / with sb) · fight in a war · also wage a war (formal)
items.meaning: take part in a war
items.example: England and France **fought a war** that lasted, on and off, for more than a hundred years.
more: The Wars of the Roses were **fought** between two branches of the same royal family.
England and France **fought a war** that lasted more than a hundred years.
items.watchOut: «Вести війну» (про країну) — fight a war, книжне wage a war. Lead — очолювати: lead an army, lead a country.

items.pattern: (UN) peacekeeping forces / troops / mission · a peacekeeper
items.meaning: soldiers sent, often by the UN, to stop fighting and keep the peace in an area
items.example: **Peacekeeping forces** from several countries were sent to keep the two sides apart.
more: My aunt worked as a nurse with UN **peacekeeping forces** in the 1990s.
The museum has a room about the history of UN **peacekeeping**.
items.watchOut: «Миротворчі сили» — peacekeeping forces, а не peaceful forces: peaceful — мирний, спокійний (a peaceful village). Миротворець — a peacekeeper.

items.pattern: the horrors of war · see / remember / experience the horrors of war
items.meaning: the terrible things that happen in a war
items.example: Wilfred Owen's poems show **the horrors of war** without any glory.
more: The old soldier in the film never talks about **the horrors** he saw.
The museum doesn't hide **the horrors of war**, so it isn't really for young children.
items.watchOut: «Жахіття війни» — the horrors of war: з the і зазвичай у множині. Horror film — фільм жахів, це інше вживання.

items.pattern: avert war / a disaster / a crisis / a strike
items.meaning: stop something bad, such as a war, from happening
items.example: The two kings met in secret and managed to **avert war**.
more: The driver's quick reaction **averted a disaster** on the motorway.
A last-minute pay deal **averted a strike** by bus drivers.
items.watchOut: Avert /əˈvɜːt/ — книжне «відвернути» щось погане: avert war / a disaster. У розмові частіше prevent або avoid. Не плутай з divert — спрямувати в об'їзд (divert traffic).

items.pattern: bring about peace / change / an end to sth · bring sth about
items.meaning: make peace happen
items.example: In the novel, a young princess **brings about peace** by marrying the son of her father's enemy.
more: Grandma finally **brought about peace** between my two uncles after years of silence.
The new head teacher **brought about** real change in the school.
items.watchOut: Bring about — спричинити, домогтися (миру, змін). Не плутай з bring up — виховувати або згадати тему. «Встановити мир» — bring about (або make) peace, а не install peace.

items.pattern: negotiate a peace agreement / deal / treaty (with sb) · peace negotiations / talks
items.meaning: discuss and agree, in official talks, how a war will end
items.example: It took two years of talks to **negotiate a peace agreement**, and it was finally signed in a small mountain village.
more: In our board game, players can **negotiate a peace agreement** instead of fighting.
We're trying to **negotiate** a lower rent with our landlord.
items.watchOut: Negotiate sth — домовитися про щось на переговорах: negotiate an agreement / a price. Negotiate with sb — вести переговори з кимось. Мирна угода — peace agreement або peace deal, а не peace contract.

items.pattern: call / declare / agree a truce / ceasefire · a ceasefire holds / breaks down
items.meaning: agree to stop fighting for a time
items.example: At Christmas 1914, soldiers in some parts of the front **called a truce** and sang carols together.
more: My brother and I **called a truce** so we could watch the film in peace.
The cat and the dog seem to have **called a truce**: they're asleep on the same sofa.
items.watchOut: Truce /truːs/ — перемир'я (часто коротке чи неофіційне), ceasefire — припинення вогню. Дієслово — call, declare або agree: a ceasefire was called.

items.pattern: sign a (peace) treaty / agreement · the Treaty of … was signed
items.meaning: officially accept a written agreement between countries by putting your name on it
items.example: After ten years of war, the two kings met on a bridge and **signed a peace treaty**.
more: The **Treaty of Versailles was signed** in 1919 in the palace's famous Hall of Mirrors.
For our history project, we wrote a pretend peace treaty, and everyone **signed it** with a feather pen.
items.watchOut: Мирний договір між країнами — a (peace) treaty /ˈtriːti/. Contract — договір у бізнесі чи на роботі (a rental contract), про мир так не кажуть.

items.pattern: a lasting peace · lasting friendship / effect / impression · long-lasting
items.meaning: peace that continues for a long time
items.example: After centuries of wars, France and Britain now enjoy a **lasting peace**.
more: The trip to Japan left a **lasting impression** on the kids.
Their **lasting friendship** began on the first day of school.
items.watchOut: «Міцний, тривалий мир» — lasting peace, а не strong peace. Lasting — той, що триває довго: a lasting impression (незабутнє враження), a lasting friendship.

items.pattern: a peace activist / campaigner · the peace movement · a peace march
items.meaning: someone who works actively against war, for example by organising marches and protests
items.example: In the 1960s, **peace activists** organised huge marches and sang songs in the streets.
more: My aunt has been a **peace activist** since her student days.
The documentary tells the story of a **peace activist** who walked across Europe.
items.watchOut: «Борець за мир» — peace activist або peace campaigner, а не peace fighter. Activist — з наголосом на перший склад: /ˈæktɪvɪst/.

items.pattern: keep the peace (between sb) · also maintain the peace (formal)
items.meaning: stop people from fighting or arguing; keep things calm
items.example: In old westerns, the sheriff's job is to **keep the peace** in a wild little town.
more: On long car journeys, Mum had to **keep the peace** between my sister and me.
Two security guards were at the wedding to **keep the peace** if anyone had too much to drink.
items.watchOut: Keep the peace — з the: не давати битися чи сваритися. Make peace (без the) — помиритися: The brothers finally made peace. «Підтримувати мир» — keep the peace, а не support the peace.

items.pattern: restore order / calm / peace · law and order
items.meaning: make a situation calm and under control again after trouble or fighting
items.example: The teacher clapped her hands twice and **restored order** in the classroom.
more: After the fans ran onto the pitch, the stewards quickly **restored order**.
It took the new captain a week to **restore order** on the ship.
items.watchOut: «Навести порядок» після бійки, заворушень чи галасу — restore order, а не make order. Прибрати в кімнаті — tidy up або tidy the room.

items.pattern: fight / have a running battle with sb (over sth) · also a long-running battle
items.meaning: a fight or argument that goes on for a long time, or a fight that moves from place to place
items.example: We've been fighting a **running battle** with our neighbours over their noisy dog.
more: Mum has a **running battle** with the slugs in her vegetable garden.
The school has a **running battle** with parents who park on the zigzag lines.
items.watchOut: Running тут не «біговий», а «тривалий, що не вщухає». Кажуть fight / have a running battle with sb. Про довгі суди й суперечки — ще a long-running battle.

items.pattern: put up a (good / brave / heroic) fight (against sth) · put up a fight
items.meaning: fight or try very hard to stop something, often when you are likely to lose
items.example: The little team from the third division **put up a brave fight** against the champions.
more: My cat **puts up a fight** every time I try to give her a pill.
Local people **put up a heroic fight** to save the old cinema, and in the end they won.
items.watchOut: «Чинити опір, мужньо боротися» — put up a fight, а не make (up) a fight чи do a fight: make up — помиритися! Часто з прикметником: a good / brave / heroic fight.

items.pattern: lose / win the battle (against / over sth / to do sth) · fight a losing battle
items.meaning: fail (or succeed) in a long struggle to achieve something
items.example: I'm **losing the battle** against the weeds in my garden.
more: After two years, the parents **won the battle** for a crossing outside the school.
Trying to keep a white sofa clean with three kids is **a losing battle**.
items.watchOut: «Програвати боротьбу» — lose the battle, а не miss the battle: miss — пропустити. Fight a losing battle — боротися без шансів на успіх.

items.pattern: offer no / little / strong resistance (to sb/sth) · also put up resistance
items.meaning: (not) try to fight or argue against someone or something
items.example: When we told Grandad he needed a new phone, he **offered surprisingly little resistance**.
more: The children **offered no resistance** when I suggested pizza for dinner.
Most people **offer little resistance** when a waiter suggests dessert.
items.watchOut: «Чинити опір» — offer або put up resistance, а не do resistance. Часто із запереченням: offered no / little resistance — не опирався.

items.pattern: be fighting for your life (in hospital) · fight for sth
items.meaning: be so ill or badly hurt that you might die
items.example: After the accident, the young cyclist **fought for her life** for a week, and now she's walking again.
more: The vet worked all night while the tiny kitten **fought for its life**.
Doctors say the climber is still **fighting for his life** after his fall.
items.watchOut: «Боротися за життя» — fight for your life: прийменник for і присвійний займенник (for his / her life), а не fight about life.

items.pattern: a price war (between shops / companies) · start a price war
items.meaning: a situation where shops or companies keep cutting prices to win customers from each other
items.example: Thanks to the **price war** between the two big supermarkets, bread has never been cheaper.
more: Two airlines started a **price war**, and flights to Spain now cost less than a train ticket.
The pizza places on our street are in a **price war**: everyone's offering two for one.
items.watchOut: «Цінова війна» — a price war: price стоїть перед іменником як прикметник, без -s і без of (не war of prices).

items.pattern: a war on / against crime / drugs / poverty · declare war on sth · fight / wage a war against sth
items.meaning: a long, organised effort, often by a government, to stop a social problem
items.uk: війна зі злочинністю (бідністю), рішуча боротьба з…
items.example: The new mayor has promised a **war on crime** in the city centre.
more: The charity has been **fighting a war against poverty** for fifty years.
The town's **war on** litter has worked: the beach is spotless now.
items.watchOut: «Війна зі злочинністю, з наркотиками» — зазвичай a war on (або against) crime / drugs. War with частіше кажуть про війну з іншою країною чи суперником: the war with France.

items.pattern: fight crime / poverty / disease / fires · also combat crime (formal)
items.meaning: try to stop or reduce crime (or another problem)
items.example: More street lights will help **fight crime** in the park at night.
more: Volunteers in our town help **fight poverty** by running a food bank.
The new fire station will help **fight fires** in the villages.
items.watchOut: «Боротися з чимось» — fight sth, без with: fight crime / poverty / a cold. Fight with sb — битися або сваритися з кимось.

warmup.explain: Спалахнула війна (пожежа, бійка) — broke out. Break down — зламатися (про машину, техніку).

warmup.uk: Мій прадід пішов в армію у вісімнадцять років.
warmup.q: My great-grandfather ___ the army at eighteen.
warmup.explain: Піти в армію — join the army (або go into the army). Go to the army — калька.

warmup.uk: Мама оголосила війну безладу в моїй кімнаті.
warmup.q: Mum has ___ war on the mess in my room.
warmup.explain: Оголосити війну — declare war on sb/sth, а не announce war.

warmup.uk: Після тижня сварок ми з братом підписали мирний договір про пульт від телевізора.
warmup.q: After a week of arguing, my brother and I signed a peace ___ about the TV remote.
warmup.explain: Мирний договір — peace treaty (або peace agreement). Contract — договір у бізнесі чи на роботі.

warmup.uk: Після великої сварки на Різдво вся родина сподівається на міцний мир.
warmup.q: After the big row at Christmas, the whole family is hoping for a ___ peace.

warmup.uk: У молодості бабуся була активісткою руху за мир.
warmup.q: When she was young, Grandma was a peace ___.
warmup.explain: Борець за мир — peace activist (або peace campaigner). Peace fighter — калька.

warmup.uk: Малий чинив запеклий опір, коли ми мили йому голову.
warmup.q: The little boy ___ a real fight when we washed his hair.
warmup.explain: Чинити опір — put up a fight. Make up — помиритися.

warmup.uk: Поліція не може боротися зі злочинністю сама.
warmup.q: The police can't ___ crime on their own.
warmup.explain: Боротися з чимось — fight sth, без with: fight crime.

A.q: Mum says a fight will ___ out if my cousins play Monopoly again.
A.explain: War breaks out — війна спалахує, раптово починається.

A.q: At Arnhem in 1944 there was ___ fighting near the bridge for days.
A.explain: Запеклі бої — fierce (або heavy) fighting, не strong і не cruel.

A.q: In the legend, the young knight was ___ prisoner in his very first battle.
A.explain: Потрапити в полон — be taken prisoner.

B.q: Nobody believed one football match could bring ___ peace between the two towns, but it did.
B.explain: Bring about peace — домогтися миру. Bring up — виховувати або згадати тему.

B.q: Both armies ___ a ceasefire on New Year's Eve.
B.explain: Оголосити припинення вогню — call (або declare, agree) a ceasefire.

B.q: It took the head waiter five minutes to ___ order after the wedding guests started throwing cake.
B.explain: Навести порядок після безладу — restore order, а не make order.

C.q: Every morning there's a ___ battle in our house over who uses the bathroom first.
C.explain: A running battle — затяжна «війна», що не вщухає.

C.q: Despite all our efforts, we ___ the battle to keep the cat out of our bedroom.
C.explain: Програти боротьбу — lose the battle. Miss — пропустити.

C.q: My boss ___ little resistance when I asked to leave early on Friday.
C.explain: Чинити опір — offer resistance; offered little resistance — майже не опиралися.

T.q: The two coffee shops are in a ___ war: both now sell a cappuccino for half the usual price.
Our town has started a war ___ dog mess in the parks.
T.explain: Війна з якоюсь проблемою — a war on (або against) sth.

T.q: Washing your hands often helps ___ infection.
T.explain: Боротися з чимось — fight sth, без with.

example.title: Game night
example.uk:
Щоп'ятниці моя родина грає в настільну гру про середньовічні королівства. Минулого тижня мій молодший брат оголосив мені війну вже в перші десять хвилин. Спершу на кордоні траплялися лише дрібні інциденти, але невдовзі почалася справжня війна. Потім мама й тато почали війну за острів, і запекла битва точилася цілу годину.

Я героїчно чинив опір, але програвав битву. Тож ми оголосили перемир'я, з'їли піцу, і мама допомогла нам домовитися про мирну угоду. Зрештою ми підписали мирний договір на паперовій серветці.

Бабуся, яка не грає, весь вечір намагалася підтримувати мир. Наступної п'ятниці ми граємо в карти.
example.en:
Every Friday my family plays a board game about medieval kingdoms. Last week my little brother [[declared war on|a3]] me in the first ten minutes. At first there were only [[minor incidents|a6]] on the border, but soon it was [[all-out war|a7]]. Then Mum and Dad [[went to war|a4]] over an island, and the [[battle raged|a13]] for an hour.

I [[put up a heroic fight|c2]], but I was [[losing the battle|c3]]. So we [[called a truce|b3]], ate some pizza, and Mum helped us [[negotiate a peace agreement|b2]]. In the end, we [[signed a peace treaty|b4]] on a paper napkin.

Grandma, who doesn't play, spent the evening trying to [[keep the peace|b7]]. Next Friday we're playing cards.
